newsitem.title: USA: GM identifies trucks to be built in Texas.
newsitem.headline: GM identifies trucks to be built in Texas.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Friday its Arlington, Texas, plant will produce Chevrolet and GMC C/K full-size pickup trucks and Tahoe and Yukon full-size sport/utility vehicles, starting in the third quarter of 1997.

The announcement is GM's first official confirmation of its product plans for the Arlington plant. Previously, the automaker had said it would convert the plant from car to truck manufacturing but had not identified specific products.
The plant now builds GM's full-size Chevrolet Caprice, Buick Roadmaster and Cadillac Fleetwood cars, which will be phased out by the end of 1996.

GM said the pickup trucks built at Arlington will all be extended-cab models with the optional third door, providing a second source for the popular vehicles. Currently, GM builds extended-cab, three-door pickups in Oshawa, Ontario.

The plant also will become the sole source for a new police version of the Chevrolet Tahoe. The less-luxurious two-wheel-drive vehicle will be equipped with a 5.7-liter V-8 engine, a heavy-duty suspension and other special equipment.
GM said the conversion of the plant to truck production will be completed in the second quarter of 1997.

Contractors have already refurbished and added over 100,000 square feet to the body shop, installed robots in the paint shop, and added an automated storage and retrieval system for painted truck bodies. Renovation of the general assembly area will begin after the end of 1996.

The project is part of a long-term plan that GM has to boost truck production to more than 50 percent of its total North American capacity. For the first six months of 1996, trucks made up about 45 percent of GM's output.

The automaker is investing about $260 million in the Arlington conversion project. GM has not disclosed the plant's future capacity, but last year, it built about 127,000 cars, a figure analysts say is well below the facility's capability.

GM spokesman Jeff Kuhlman said the 1998-model-year C/K pickups and four-door Tahoe and Yukon trucks scheduled for Arlington will be carry-over vehicles from the current product lines. The automaker is scheduled to introduce redesigned full-size pickup trucks for the 1999 model year.
The Tahoe police package production will start in the summer of 1997, GM said.

"Conversion of the Arlington plant is the latest in a number of steps we've taken over the past several years to increase our production capacity for full-size trucks," said Michael Grimaldi, GM vice president and vehicle line executive for full-size trucks. "It allows us to build more of the products customers are demanding."
At a press conference Friday at the Texas State Fair, Grimaldi predicted that the worldwide truck market would grow to 20 million units from 15 million in the next several years.
Truck sales in North America alone are expected to increase to 50 percent from 43 percent of the current market over the same time frame, he said.
